title: Jammu Station On Alert After Pigeon With 'IED Blast Threat' Caught Near India-Pakistan Border | India News - News18
text: Jammu Railway Station was put on alert after a pigeon was caught near the India-Pakistan international border, with a note threatening an “IED blast", officials said on Thursday. The Border Security Force caught the pigeon in the Khatmarian area of RS Pura with a paper tied to its leg. The paper tied to the pigeon read, “Jammu Station IED Blast". The BSF informed the Jammu and Kashmir Police about the threat message, after which an alert was issued at the railway station, officials said. The incident comes days after the security forces caught a suspicious pigeon in the border area on August 18. The bird was spotted by a patrol team in suspicious circumstances near Forward Defense Post-69, close to Kathmaria BOP, under the 07 Battalion of the BSF, The Daily Jagran reported. The slip that was recovered had messages written in both Urdu and English. It read: “Kashmir Hamara Hai" (Kashmir is ours), “Waqt Aa Gaya Hai, Aa Jayega" (The time has come, it will come), and “Jammu Station IED Blast", the report said. The BSF and other security agencies were investigating whether the pigeon flew on the Indian side from across the border.
